parties: Emirates NBD Bank (acquirer) | RBL Bank Limited (target)
headline: Emirates NBD Bank Posts Open Offer Advertisement on RBL Bank; SEBI Takeover Framework Compliance Closure
sum: Emirates NBD Bank has formally closed its open offer on RBL Bank Limited via NSE post-offer advertisement (19 June 2026), signalling completion of the mandatory disclosure phase under SEBI's substantial acquisition and takeover regulations. The filing marks regulatory closure of the offer period and compliance with Regulations 2011, with residual CCI and RBI clearances for cross-border banking consolidation potentially outstanding.
implication: Post-offer advertisement filing is the formal regulatory closure gate under SEBI SAST Regulations 2011; banking sector M&A is unusually complex due to dual RBI-SEBI jurisdiction and CCI foreign investment review-practitioners must monitor whether any residual RBI circular on foreign acquisition of banking shares or CCI gun-jumping assessment remains enforceable post-completion.
detail: Emirates NBD Bank, a UAE-domiciled lender, triggered SEBI's substantial acquisition thresholds in RBL Bank (a Tier-II private sector bank headquartered in Mumbai), necessitating an open offer under the Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers (SAST) Regulations, 2011. The post-offer advertisement filed on 19 June 2026 (dated 18 June 2026) fulfils the mandatory disclosure requirement once the offer period concludes, per Schedule VI of the Regulations. The advertisement contains final offer terms (price per share, total consideration, acceptances received) and post-offer shareholding; residual regulatory clearances from RBI (banking sector FDI framework and any moratorium on foreign acquisition) and CCI (if cross-border concentration thresholds are triggered) may condition final delisting or consolidation.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Schedule VI
framework.note: Post-offer advertisement and closure disclosure; mandatory filing within prescribed days of offer conclusion.

framework.ref: SEBI SAST Regulations 2011, Regulation 3(d) & Schedule II
framework.note: Trigger thresholds (25% direct acquisition or convertible holding) and open offer obligation for substantial acquirers.

framework.ref: Banking Regulation Act, 1949, Section 45 & RBI Regulations on Acquisition of shares in Indian banks
framework.note: RBI approval for foreign acquisition of shares in an Indian bank; may include cross-border FDI ceilings and sector-specific conditions.
CCI gun-jumping and concentration review for cross-border banking consolidation; filing may be triggered if combined entity exceeds CCI thresholds.
FEMA approval for foreign direct investment by Emirates NBD in Indian banking shares; RBI's Investment Committee role.

framework.ref: RBI Master Circular on Foreign Investment in India (latest edition)
framework.note: Sector-specific caps and conditions on foreign ownership in banking entities; may limit post-acquisition shareholding or require regulatory approval for consolidation.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Section 230 & Chapter XX (Compromise & Arrangement)
framework.note: If scheme of arrangement or merger is contemplated post-takeover, NCLT sanction may be required; distinct from open offer regime.
If post-offer shareholding enables compulsory delisting, SEBI Delisting Regulations become applicable; separate public announcement framework.

conditions: Open offer acceptance by target shareholders during prescribed offer period
Post-offer shareholding and securities delivery via depositories (NSDL/CDSL)
Residual RBI approval for foreign acquisition of banking shares (if not already cleared pre-offer)
CCI assessment for cross-border concentration (if triggered by combined market share or asset thresholds)
RBI policy clearance for consolidation or integration post-acquisition
approvals: SEBI (open offer under SAST Regulations 2011) - Confirmed (post-offer filing indicates closure)
RBI (Banking Regulation Act, 1949 & FDI framework) - Status unclear; may be pre-offer or post-completion
CCI (Competition Act, 2010) - Status unclear; may require separate filing if thresholds met
structure.novel: Cross-border banking acquisition (UAE acquirer into Tier-II Indian bank) under SEBI SAST framework with potential dual RBI-SEBI jurisdiction and CCI review; the post-offer advertisement closure (rather than continuation via scheme) suggests open offer path to acquisition (vs. scheme of arrangement alternative).

triggers.note: Substantial acquisition of 25%+ direct or convertible stake mandates open offer; Emirates NBD's acquisition appears to have crossed this threshold.
Foreign acquisition of banking shares requires RBI approval; FDI eligibility and sector caps apply.
Cross-border acquisition may trigger CCI review if combined asset/turnover thresholds are exceeded or market concentration concerns arise.
Capital account transaction (FDI into banking) requires RBI authorization; foreign investor remittance and repatriation norms apply.

triggers.law: RBI Foreign Investment Master Circular (current edition)
triggers.note: Sector-specific cap on foreign direct investment in banking; may restrict final shareholding % or impose integration conditions.
